facts.statement: A large articulated skeleton was discovered in 1996 by a Belgian-Chinese expedition in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of China.
facts.quote: In 1996, a Belgian-Chinese expedition discovered a large, articulated skeleton in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of China.

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named the specimen IMM 96BM3/1 as Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus in 1999.
facts.quote: In 1999, Pascal Godefroit and colleagues named this specimen, accessioned as IMM 96BM3/1, as a new species of the genus Pinacosaurus, P. mephistocephalus.

facts.statement: Paul Penkalski transferred Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus to the new genus Eopinacosaurus in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred P. mephistocephalus to a new genus, Eopinacosaurus.

facts.statement: The specific name mephistocephalus refers to "devilish" squamosal horns.
facts.quote: The specific name is a contraction of Mephistopheles and the Greek κεφαλή, kephalè, "head", in reference to the "devilish" squamosal horns.

facts.statement: The genus contains a single species, Eopinacosaurus mephistocephalus.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Eopinacosaurus mephistocephalus, which was originally assigned to the coeval genus Pinacosaurus.

facts.statement: Fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) Bayan Mandahu Formation of China and the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian age) Bayan Mandahu Formation of China and Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Eopinacosaurus is classified as a member of the ankylosaurid subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Eopinacosaurus is regarded as a member of the ankylosaurid subfamily Ankylosaurinae

facts.statement: Eopinacosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia, family Ankylosauridae, and subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ankylosaurinae Family: Ankylosauridae Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Eopinacosaurus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus was a junior synonym of Pinacosaurus grangeri.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that P. mephistocephalus were a junior synonym of P. grangeri.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have recovered Eopinacosaurus in a variable position within the clade relative to the type species of Pinacosaurus.
facts.quote: although phylogenetic analyses including it (as "Pinacosaurus" mephistocephalus) since its description have recovered it in a variable position within the clade and in relation to the Pinacosaurus type species, P. grangeri.

rejected.statement: Eopinacosaurus is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid armored dinosaur meaning "dawn Pinacosaurus".
rejected.quote: Eopinacosaurus (meaning "dawn Pinacosaurus") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid armored dinosaur
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid armored dinosaur'
